missing: No control exists for environment variables under --det: they are neither normalized, nor recorded as events, nor written in the trace header. Two runs that differ in TZ, LANG, LC_ALL, HOME, USER, CI and a custom variable give byte-identical fingerprints for the tests that read them. CONTROLS is only order,seeds,hashseed,bytecode,time,fs,net.
evidence: python/detpy/_level0.py:22 (engine@claude/release-1) CONTROLS tuple; RAN: `TZ=Asia/Tokyo MY_FLAG=bad pytest --det` vs `TZ=America/New_York pytest --det` => tests/test_fs.py::test_env fingerprint 5644e21c... in both, outcome failed vs passed (notes PY3-001)

missing: When a test outcome differs between two --det runs because of an environment variable, the verifier cannot say why: it reports `outcome-only ... the cause is a source Level 0 does not observe`. The promise (exact event where runs diverge) is not kept for env-caused flakiness, the most common cross-machine cause.
evidence: RAN: `python -m detpy verify e1.jsonl e2.jsonl` => `NOT-COVERED tests/test_fs.py::test_env [outcome-only] outcomes=failed,passed ... identical observed events, different outcome` (notes PY3-002)

missing: No timezone control under --det: the virtual clock fixes the UTC instant only; datetime.now(), time.localtime(), time.strftime, time.tzname follow the machine TZ. Same commit, same seed: datetime.now() is 17:33 with TZ=Asia/Tokyo and 03:33 with TZ=America/New_York, and a test asserting on the local hour fails on one machine and passes on the other with identical fingerprints.
evidence: RAN: tests/test_tzdep.py::test_tz_hour `assert 17 < 12` failed under TZ=Asia/Tokyo --det, passed under TZ=America/New_York --det; verify => [outcome-only]. docs/LIMITS.md C7 (`time.localtime() depends on TZ`)

missing: No locale control under --det: LANG/LC_* are not pinned, locale.getlocale()/setlocale(LC_ALL,'') results are not normalized or recorded. Run 1 printed LOCALE ('C','UTF-8'), run 2 (LANG=de_DE.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C) printed (None,None); fingerprints identical (44c0e26c...).
evidence: RAN: tests/test_fs.py::test_locale_tz under two environments, same fingerprint 44c0e26c5f70a32a7f2a24ba566aac6e; `grep -rn locale python/detpy` => only runtime_id.py (cache key), nothing in _level0/clock

missing: No scheduling control for Python on release-1: no --det-async, no --det-threads, no Source::Sched event ever emitted by the Python shell. asyncio ready-queue order, timers, executor completions and thread switches follow the real scheduler. Block 3 (ROADMAP: CLOSED 2026-11-18 with `--det --det-threads`) lives only on origin/claude/l1-threads-fix, which is not an ancestor of release-1.
evidence: `pytest --help | grep det-threads` => nothing; `grep -rn 'det-threads|det_async|aio' python/detpy` => nothing (engine@claude/release-1); `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/claude/l1-threads-fix origin/claude/release-1` => not ancestor; python/detpy/aio.py exists only on l1 branches

missing: asyncio loop time is not virtual: BaseEventLoop.time() is forced to the real monotonic clock, so loop.time(), call_later/call_at deadlines and asyncio.timeout differ from run to run (LOOPTIME 1010.77 vs 1020.37) while time.time() in the same coroutine is virtual: two inconsistent clocks inside one test.
evidence: python/detpy/clock.py: `patcher.set(asyncio.base_events.BaseEventLoop, "time", lambda self: real_monotonic())` (engine@claude/release-1); RAN tests/test_time.py::test_loop_time twice under --det: loop.time() 1010.770980256 vs 1020.369366521; docs/LIMITS.md C3

missing: time.process_time(), time.thread_time(), os.times() and resource.getrusage() are not virtualised and not recorded: values differ every run (process_time 0.873 vs 0.914; os.times().elapsed 17180579.69 vs 17180589.29) and a test asserting on CPU time stays flaky with an identical fingerprint.
evidence: RAN tests/test_time.py::test_time_apis twice under --det (notes PY3-007); python/detpy/clock.py `fakes` dict lists only time,time_ns,monotonic(_ns),perf_counter(_ns),sleep,localtime,gmtime,ctime,asctime,strftime,clock_gettime(_ns); docs/LIMITS.md C7

missing: File timestamps are real under --det: a file written by a test gets st_mtime from the kernel clock (1795163580.8) while time.time() returns the virtual epoch (1795163542.0), so `mtime <= time.time()` style assertions and cache-freshness code see a file from the future; the value differs every run and is not recorded.
evidence: RAN tests/test_time.py::test_file_mtime: `MTIME 1795163580.8495526 NOW 1795163542.000001` then `MTIME 1795163590.4416487 NOW 1795163542.000001`; docs/LIMITS.md C7, F1

missing: os.urandom, secrets, uuid.uuid4 and random.SystemRandom are not deterministic under plain --det (observed only): each run prints different values and every test that uses them is reported NOT-COVERED [entropy] by the verifier. The user must know to add --det-urandom; --det alone does not keep 'same inputs, same result'.
evidence: RAN twice: RANDVALS sysr 0.5052 vs 0.5537, ur 39cefb45 vs 2c742c02, u4 66b885ee.. vs df6b5313..; `detpy verify` => `NOT-COVERED tests/test_random.py::test_random_apis [entropy]`; python/detpy/seeds.py docstring (observed, not controlled)
decide_for: Crypto tests need real entropy; --det-urandom exists as an opt-in.
decide_against: uuid4/secrets are used for ids in ordinary tests everywhere; a default that leaves them random makes many tests 'not covered' and non-reusable; the safe default could be deterministic with an opt-out for crypto tests.

missing: uuid.uuid1() is not controlled even with --det-urandom: it mixes the real clock (libuuid / C time) and node id; values differ on every run and no event is recorded for it.
evidence: RAN `pytest --det --det-urandom` twice: u1 106e59f6-e4bd-11f1-913f-a380c90b1617 vs 12b9e900-e4bd-11f1-bc53-bdd2e5d5dc6e while uuid4/secrets/urandom were equal; docs/LIMITS.md K1 mentions uuid1 only for the cache

missing: numpy is seeded only if it is already imported when a test starts: a test that imports numpy lazily (inside the test body or via a lazily imported library) gets unseeded np.random.rand() and default_rng() values, different every run.
evidence: RAN tests/test_random.py::test_random_apis (import numpy inside the test) twice under --det: np 0.4383 vs 0.7994, np_rng 0.8611 vs 0.7262; python/detpy/seeds.py start_test: `np = sys.modules.get("numpy")`; docs/LIMITS.md R4

missing: numpy generators built explicitly without a seed, np.random.Generator(np.random.PCG64()) and np.random.RandomState(), are not seeded by --det (only the global state and default_rng() are): values differ per run unless --det-urandom is added.

missing: Only random and numpy are seeded. torch, tensorflow, jax and Faker's own generators have no control (documented limit R4): for ML projects, the main Python audience, --det does not make random-dependent tests reproducible.

missing: False divergence in every numpy project: detpy's own per-test reseed (np.random.seed) triggers numpy's lazy import of numpy/random/_pickle.py, whose os.urandom read is recorded as event #0 of whichever test runs first in the process. missing: Replay does not validate the request: when the test now sends a different request (other URL path, other Authorization header) the recorded response of the old request is served; only a `replay.mismatch` event is written in the trace, nothing is printed and nothing fails. missing: The virtual-day rule (brain DECISIONS 2026-11-19: epoch = today 00:00 UTC, keyed by day, plus a nightly real-clock run, 'same rule for Python, Node and Go') is not implemented for Python: the epoch is the HEAD commit time kept by the cache for up to 30 days (--det-cache-epoch-window), and there is no real-clock run option or workflow (Go has go-nightly-real-clock.yml).
